# markfmt grammar cases

Each case gives the expected HTML of a corpus example whose meaning
markfmt's grammar changes, or whose meaning cmark and commonmark.js
disagree on. A `grammar-differs.txt` file names the case by its section
(design 11.2). The test HTML renderer writes nothing for front
matter.

## commonmark 96

Front matter takes the first three lines.

```````````````````````````````` example
---
Foo
---
Bar
---
Baz
.
<h2>Bar</h2>
<p>Baz</p>
````````````````````````````````

## commonmark 98

The two lines are empty front matter.

```````````````````````````````` example
---
---
.
````````````````````````````````

## commonmark-js-regression 25

cmark 0.31.1 makes the list of Case 7 loose: the blank line in the HTML
block of the first item is the last line of that item. commonmark.js reads
the blank line as part of the HTML block and keeps the list tight. markfmt
follows cmark (design 2, 5.6). The expected HTML is the output of
`cmark --unsafe` 0.31.1.

```````````````````````````````` example
## Case 1

- > a
  >
- b


## Case 2

- > - a
  >
- b


## Case 3

- > > a
  >
- b


## Case 4

- > # a
  >
- b


## Case 5

- ```
  The following line is part of code block.

- b

## Case 6

-     The following line is **not** part of code block.
      
- b

## Case 7

- <pre>The following line is part of HTML block.

- </pre>
- b
.
<h2>Case 1</h2>
<ul>
<li>
<blockquote>
<p>a</p>
</blockquote>
</li>
<li>b</li>
</ul>
<h2>Case 2</h2>
<ul>
<li>
<blockquote>
<ul>
<li>a</li>
</ul>
</blockquote>
</li>
<li>b</li>
</ul>
<h2>Case 3</h2>
<ul>
<li>
<blockquote>
<blockquote>
<p>a</p>
</blockquote>
</blockquote>
</li>
<li>b</li>
</ul>
<h2>Case 4</h2>
<ul>
<li>
<blockquote>
<h1>a</h1>
</blockquote>
</li>
<li>b</li>
</ul>
<h2>Case 5</h2>
<ul>
<li>
<pre><code>The following line is part of code block.

</code></pre>
</li>
<li>b</li>
</ul>
<h2>Case 6</h2>
<ul>
<li>
<pre><code>The following line is **not** part of code block.
</code></pre>
</li>
<li>
<p>b</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h2>Case 7</h2>
<ul>
<li>
<pre>The following line is part of HTML block.

</li>
<li>
</pre>
</li>
<li>
<p>b</p>
</li>
</ul>
````````````````````````````````

## github 10

Every backtick run of the same length after an unmatched run can close a
code span, as the spec text and commonmark.js give (`../dialect.md`).
GitHub leaves the second code span as text.

```````````````````````````````` example
a `` b `c` d `e`
.
<p>a `` b <code>c</code> d <code>e</code></p>
````````````````````````````````

## github 11

A title that other characters follow on its line is not the title of the
definition, as the spec text and commonmark.js give (CM 210,
`../dialect.md`). GitHub keeps the title.

```````````````````````````````` example
[foo]: /url
"title"ok

[foo]
.
<p>&quot;title&quot;ok</p>
<p><a href="/url">foo</a></p>
````````````````````````````````

## github 13

VT and FF end a link destination, as in cmark 0.31.1 (`../dialect.md`).
GitHub takes them into the destination.

```````````````````````````````` example
[a](bc)

[a](bc)
.
<p>[a](bc)</p>
<p>[a](bc)</p>
````````````````````````````````

## github 14

Unicode symbols count as punctuation for flanking (`../dialect.md`). GitHub
counts only Unicode P and ASCII punctuation.

```````````````````````````````` example
£_a_£
.
<p>£<em>a</em>£</p>
````````````````````````````````

## github 15

An HTML block of kind 4 starts with `<!` and any ASCII letter
(`../dialect.md`). GitHub needs an uppercase letter.

```````````````````````````````` example
<!doctype html>
.
<!doctype html>
````````````````````````````````

## github 16

An HTML block of kind 7 does not start on a lazy candidate line, so both
lines continue the paragraph in the block quote (`../dialect.md`). GitHub
closes the block quote and starts an HTML block.

```````````````````````````````` example
> a
<del>
*b*
.
<blockquote>
<p>a
<del>
<em>b</em></p>
</blockquote>
````````````````````````````````

## github 17

`search` is in the tag list of HTML block kind 6, so it interrupts the
paragraph (`../dialect.md`). GitHub reads it as kind 7, which does not.

```````````````````````````````` example
a
<search>
*b*
.
<p>a</p>
<search>
*b*
````````````````````````````````

## github 18

`source` is not in the tag list of HTML block kind 6, so it does not
interrupt the paragraph (`../dialect.md`). GitHub reads it as kind 6.

```````````````````````````````` example
a
<source>
*b*
.
<p>a
<source>
<em>b</em></p>
````````````````````````````````

## github 19

`<!-- c -- d --->` is a raw HTML comment under CommonMark 0.31.2
(`../dialect.md`). GitHub's older comment grammar reads it as text.

```````````````````````````````` example
a <!--> b --> <!-- c -- d --->
.
<p>a <!--> b --&gt; <!-- c -- d ---></p>
````````````````````````````````

## commonmark 602

The text between `<` and `>` is not an autolink, and the URL in it is an
extended URL autolink. The expected HTML is the normalized output of the GitHub
Markdown API, 2026-09-13, which equals the output of cmark-gfm with the
autolink extension.

```````````````````````````````` example
<https://foo.bar/baz bim>
.
<p>&lt;<a href="https://foo.bar/baz">https://foo.bar/baz</a> bim&gt;</p>
````````````````````````````````

## commonmark 608

The text between `<` and `>` is not an autolink, and the URL in it is an
extended URL autolink. The expected HTML is the normalized output of the GitHub
Markdown API, 2026-09-13, which equals the output of cmark-gfm with the
autolink extension.

```````````````````````````````` example
< https://foo.bar >
.
<p>&lt; <a href="https://foo.bar">https://foo.bar</a> &gt;</p>
````````````````````````````````

## commonmark 611

A URL is an extended URL autolink. The expected HTML is the normalized output of the GitHub
Markdown API, 2026-09-13, which equals the output of cmark-gfm with the
autolink extension.

```````````````````````````````` example
https://example.com
.
<p><a href="https://example.com">https://example.com</a></p>
````````````````````````````````

## commonmark 606

The text between `<` and `>` is not an autolink, and its decoded text holds
an extended email autolink. The expected HTML is the normalized output of the GitHub
Markdown API, 2026-09-13, which equals the output of cmark-gfm with the
autolink extension.

```````````````````````````````` example
<foo\+@bar.example.com>
.
<p>&lt;<a href="mailto:foo+@bar.example.com">foo+@bar.example.com</a>&gt;</p>
````````````````````````````````

## commonmark 612

An email address is an extended email autolink. The expected HTML is the normalized output of the GitHub
Markdown API, 2026-09-13, which equals the output of cmark-gfm with the
autolink extension.

```````````````````````````````` example
foo@bar.example.com
.
<p><a href="mailto:foo@bar.example.com">foo@bar.example.com</a></p>
````````````````````````````````

## github 20

VT and FF at the ends of an info string are trimmed, as in cmark 0.31.1
(`../dialect.md`). GitHub keeps them, and its sanitizer writes VT as
U+FFFD.

```````````````````````````````` example
~~~a
x
~~~

~~~a
y
~~~
.
<pre><code class="language-a">x
</code></pre>
<pre><code class="language-a">y
</code></pre>
````````````````````````````````

## github 21

A link label has at most 999 characters, as the spec text and
commonmark.js give (`../dialect.md`). GitHub counts at most 1000 bytes, so
a label of 600 `é` is not a label.

```````````````````````````````` example
[éééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééé]: /u

[éééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééé]
.
<p><a href="/u">éééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééééé</a></p>
````````````````````````````````

## github 22

VT and FF in a link label are whitespace, as in cmark 0.31.1
(`../dialect.md`). GitHub keeps them in the label, so no definition
matches.

```````````````````````````````` example
[a]

[a]: /u

[b]

[b]: /v
.
<p><a href="/u">a</a></p>
<p><a href="/v">b</a></p>
````````````````````````````````

## github 23

cmark 0.31.1 opens every list item that starts on a line (`../dialect.md`).
cmark-gfm opens at most 99 blocks on a line. The expected HTML is the output of
`cmark --unsafe` 0.31.1.

## github 29

The decoded text of a footnote reference starts with `^`, so a caret that is
a backslash escape or an entity reference makes a reference
(`../dialect.md`). GitHub garbles the text.

```````````````````````````````` example
a[\^1] b[&#94;1]

[^1]: x
.
<p>a<sup class="footnote-ref"><a href="#fn-1" id="fnref-1" data-footnote-ref>1</a></sup> b<sup class="footnote-ref"><a href="#fn-1" id="fnref-1-2" data-footnote-ref>1</a></sup></p>
<section class="footnotes" data-footnotes>
<ol>
<li id="fn-1">
<p>x <a href="#fnref-1" class="footnote-backref" data-footnote-backref data-footnote-backref-idx="1" aria-label="Back to reference 1">↩</a> <a href="#fnref-1-2" class="footnote-backref" data-footnote-backref data-footnote-backref-idx="1-2" aria-label="Back to reference 1-2">↩<sup class="footnote-ref">2</sup></a></p>
</li>
</ol>
</section>
````````````````````````````````

## github 37

The label of a footnote reference can hold a line ending, which no definition
label has, so the reference is unresolved and written as its text
(`../dialect.md`). GitHub garbles the text.

```````````````````````````````` example
a[^b
c]

[^b]: x
.
<p>a[^b
c]</p>
````````````````````````````````
